name: Kenya
summary: A British colony that won independence in 1963 after the Mau Mau uprising; a regional hub for business, tourism and long-distance running.

knownFor.label: Wangari Maathai
knownFor.note: First African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize.

location.value: East Africa on the Indian Ocean; about 580,000 km².

terrain.value: The coast, the Rift Valley, highlands with snow-capped Mount Kenya, and savanna.

climate.value: Hot and humid on the coast, dry in the north, and cooler and wetter in the central highlands, with two rainy seasons.

resources.value: Tea, coffee and cut flowers for export, plus wildlife tourism, geothermal power and farmland.

disasters.value: Droughts in the north and east, and floods during the rainy seasons, have repeatedly caused hunger and displacement.

population.value: More than 54 million (2026), the seventh-most populous country in Africa.

urbanisation.value: Nairobi is the capital and largest city; Mombasa, a port on Mombasa Island, is the second-largest and oldest.

disease.value: Malaria and HIV have been the main diseases; vaccination and treatment programmes have cut deaths since the 2000s.

migration.value: Kenya hosts large refugee camps at Dadaab and Kakuma, mainly for people from Somalia and South Sudan.

economicBase.value: Agriculture is the largest sector (tea, coffee and other crops); also tourism and services.

tradeRoutes.value: The port of Mombasa is the main gateway for East Africa, linked inland by road and railway to Uganda and beyond.

moneyAndTax.value: The Kenyan shilling, introduced in 1966 to replace the East African shilling; taxes include VAT and income tax.

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

governmentType.value: A presidential republic with a two-chamber parliament and 47 county governments (since 2013).

keyRulers.value: Jomo Kenyatta. Daniel arap Moi. Mwai Kibaki. Later and present leaders are not named here.

succession.value: The president is elected; the disputed 2007 election led to violence in which more than 1,000 people died.

institutions.value: The 2010 constitution set up counties, a Bill of Rights and an independent judiciary.

stability.value: The Mau Mau uprising (from 1952) before independence; disputed elections in 2007 and 2017.

eliteConflict.value: Competition between political parties and leaders.

armyAndTech.value: The Kenya Defence Forces (army, navy and air force), plus a large police service.

majorWars.value: The Mau Mau uprising against British rule (1952–60), and operations against al-Shabaab in Somalia since 2011.

territoryChange.value: Kenya’s borders have stayed the same since independence; the sea border with Somalia was settled by the International Court of Justice in 2021.

alliancesRivals.value: A member of the East African Community; joined its common market in 2010.

inventions.value: M-Pesa mobile banking, launched in 2007 by Vodafone and Safaricom.

scienceEducation.value: The University of Nairobi (1970 as a full university) and free primary schooling from 2003.

openness.value: Open to trade and foreign investment, with periods of restriction.

communicationTransport.value: The Standard Gauge Railway links Mombasa with Nairobi (opened 2017); the M-Pesa mobile money system began here in 2007.

religion.value: Mostly Christian (about 85%), with a Muslim minority.

languageWriting.value: Swahili and English are the official languages, with over 40 other languages such as Kikuyu, Luo and Kalenjin.

artsArchitecture.value: Novels and plays in English, Swahili and Gikuyu, Maasai beadwork, and the Swahili coast buildings of Lamu and Mombasa.

socialStructure.value: Kikuyu, Luhya, Kalenjin, Luo and others.

sharedIdentity.value: Kenyans hold a national identity but many politics follow ethnic and regional lines.

dailyLife.value: Many families live in villages or city flats; ugali (maize meal) with sukuma wiki (greens) is a common meal.

neighbours.value: Tanzania, Uganda, South Sudan, Ethiopia, Somalia.

ideasReligions.value: Swahili coastal culture, Christianity (the majority), Islam on the coast, and traditional beliefs.

colonisation.value: A British protectorate from 1895 and Kenya Colony from 1920; independent in 1963.

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

outcome.value: Kenya continues as an independent republic.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
